B.strength: Direct address to Yahweh, created-human dignity/crowning and dominion comparable with Genesis image/dominion make God a coherent contextual reading.
B.objection: Neither formal noun morphology nor source-language primacy rules out plural divine beings. A Greek angels interpretation can render the same Hebrew; no compulsory God sense.

A.strength: Divine/heavenly beings is a live Hebrew semantic possibility and coheres with the selected Greek angels rendering.
A.objection: Heavenly specifies the type/location of beings beyond the bare noun; this does not by itself outperform God in this Psalm's creation/royal context.

root_assessment.verdict: Retain current main English provisionally; no demonstrated main-English superiority. Correct the false Hiphil and compulsory-God rationale in a separate full-record application.
root_assessment.source_outcome: Keep pinned WLC; no changed Hebrew letters, vowels or securely discriminating early noun evidence.

review.verdict: Tie, with a modest contextual advantage for B insufficient to require replacing A.

A.strongest_case: Elohim can denote divine/superhuman beings; heavenly beings avoids restricting that category to angels and accords with selected Greek interpretation.
A.strongest_objection: Heavenly is interpretive and the plural excludes God; not uniquely literal or ambiguity-preserving.

B.strongest_case: Humanity small beside Creator's heavens receives honor and authority over earthly works; God fits naturally. Genesis image/dominion is compatible contextual inference.
B.strongest_objection: Specifies singular deity despite available divine-being sense and Greek interpretation; plausibility is not exclusivity.
